title: AgentRun: Open-Source Sandbox for AI Agents
summary: AgentRun provides a secure, isolated sandbox for executing AI-generated Python code. Developers can evaluate model outputs without risking infrastructure.
body_markdown:
## Integrating AgentRun into existing automation workflows


AgentRun functions as a durable execution platform that converts high-level instructions into isolated code runs within a secure environment, preserving state across interruptions.


By decoupling the reasoning engine from the execution shell, developers ensure that a logic error or malicious injection in the model output cannot compromise the host system's file structure.


### Triggering code execution with HTTP requests


To trigger code execution, the automation platform sends a structured POST request to the AgentRun endpoint containing the script and its required dependencies.


This synchronous connection returns the standard output or error logs directly to the workflow, meaning the next step in the sequence can immediately use that data for conditional logic.


Because AgentRun handles the container lifecycle automatically, the workflow designer does not need to manage server spin-up times or teardown scripts.


### Managing external execution providers


AgentRun serves as a unified management layer that can orchestrate code across various third-party sandbox providers. While it includes a native Docker-based runner for local use, it also acts as a gateway to specialized environments like E2B, Daytona, and Modal.


E2B and Daytona provide cloud-based sandboxes specifically optimized for AI agents, offering fast startup times and pre-configured development environments. Modal focuses on serverless GPU and high-performance compute tasks, allowing the agent to scale horizontally for heavy data processing.


By using AgentRun as the central controller, developers avoid vendor lock-in and can route tasks to the environment best suited for the specific script.


The system manages the authentication and communication with these providers, presenting a consistent API to the AI agent regardless of where the code actually runs.


The breadth of environments AgentRun can target demonstrates the versatility of this connection.

This setup allows a single automation flow to move from a cloud-based Python script to a local desktop action without changing the API structure.


### Configuring OpenAI-compatible providers for agent logic


AgentRun utilizes an OpenAI-compatible API format to receive instructions from frontier models, allowing it to integrate with any provider that supports standard tool-calling schemas.


When using a reasoning-heavy model like Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra, the agent identifies when a task requires computation and formats the code block for the AgentRun tool.


You will not find this in the logs, because the failure never raised an error.


This compatibility means developers can swap a high-latency model for a faster alternative like Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite or GPT-6 Luna simply by updating the base URL and API key in the configuration.


### AgentRun support for Model Context Protocol servers


The Model Context Protocol (MCP) acts as a standardized interface for AgentRun to pull in external data sources, such as documentation or database schemas, before executing code.


By connecting to an MCP server, the agent gains a precise map of the environment it is working in, which reduces the likelihood of the model hallucinating non-existent library functions.


This protocol-based extension ensures that as new tools are added to the ecosystem, AgentRun can consume their capabilities without requiring a custom integration for every unique data source.
